text: Twenty-four lessons each taught one piece of running a governance program. This closing lesson isn't a twenty-fifth concept — it's the exercise that makes you assemble the other twenty-four into one packet you could hand to a real governance council.

Steps one through three come from Chapter 1: name the domain and what's out of scope, list three affected stakeholders and who chairs the council, and name one steward with one specific responsibility nobody currently owns.

Steps four through six: write one real policy and who holds the decision rights to change it, describe a three-step dispute and escalation workflow, and name exactly two KPIs tied directly to the original pain — not a long list.

Steps seven through nine: name the group most likely to resist and one targeted fix for them, sort three next steps into now, next, and later, and write one sentence defending the budget plus the single weakest dimension today.

Read the finished packet as a whole. Solid charter but vague policy means it isn't ready to launch yet. Solid steps one through seven but a hard step eight means it's genuinely in the sustaining phase. And a weak dimension that keeps repeating isn't a one-time finding — it belongs on the roadmap every cycle until it moves.

Congratulations — that packet is Data Governance Program Management, complete, charter through sustaining. The Data Governance career path continues next with Data Governance Architecture, moving from how a program is run to how the systems and platforms underneath it are actually structured to support it.
